# Puncturing System with Enhanced Safety Features

## Overview

The present invention relates to a puncturing system designed for medical applications requiring safe and controlled access to internal body structures. The system incorporates a multi-component architecture that not only facilitates precise puncturing but also provides an integrated safety mechanism to protect the puncturing needle after use.

## System Architecture

### Outer Tubular Body

The puncturing system comprises an outer tubular body that is specifically configured to remain positioned within a body part of a living being throughout the duration of the medical procedure. This outer tubular body serves as a stable, fixed reference structure and defines a working lumen through which the other functional components of the system are guided. Its design ensures that it maintains a secure and consistent position relative to the target anatomical site during use.

### Inner Tubular Body

Housed within the working lumen of the outer tubular body is at least one inner tubular body. This inner tubular body is arranged such that it can be guided through the outer tubular body's working lumen and is capable of longitudinal displacement relative to it. In other words, the inner tubular body can slide axially forward and backward within the outer tubular body, allowing for controlled, incremental movement during the puncturing procedure. This sliding relationship between the inner and outer tubular bodies forms a critical part of the invention's functional design.

### Puncturing Needle

A puncturing needle is guided through a dedicated puncture lumen formed within the inner tubular body. Similar to the relationship between the inner and outer tubular bodies, the inner tubular body is likewise configured to be longitudinally displaceable with respect to the puncturing needle. This means that once the needle is positioned, the inner tubular body can move independently along the length of the needle, enabling a coordinated, sequential deployment of the system's components during the puncturing process.

## Operational Sequence and Safety Mechanism

The puncturing needle possesses a puncturing section designed to penetrate the target body part. During the procedure, this puncturing section is advanced through the body part until it punctures through and protrudes from the patient-side end of the assembly.

Once this puncture has been achieved and the puncturing section extends beyond the patient-side end, the inner tubular body is configured to move partially out of the outer tubular body. This controlled advancement of the inner tubular body serves a critical safety function: as the inner tubular body extends outward, it is able to receive and enclose at least a portion of the now-exposed, protruding puncturing section within its own puncture lumen.

## Advantages

By enclosing the protruding portion of the needle's puncturing section immediately after the puncture is completed, the system substantially reduces the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to medical personnel or the patient. This design provides an integrated, mechanically actuated safety covering that requires no separate or additional device, thereby streamlining the post-puncture workflow while significantly enhancing the overall safety profile of the puncturing procedure. The coordinated telescoping movement between the outer tubular body, the inner tubular body, and the puncturing needle thus achieves both effective tissue penetration and reliable needle protection within a single, integrated system.

# Puncturing System with Enhanced Safety Mechanism

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a puncturing system for medical applications, particularly to a device configured for safe puncturing procedures within a body part, wherein the system incorporates multiple coaxially arranged tubular components designed to protect medical personnel and patients from inadvertent needle-stick injuries following the puncturing procedure.

## Background

Puncturing devices used in various medical procedures, such as vascular access, biopsy, or drainage procedures, typically involve a needle that is advanced through tissue to reach a target location within a body part. A significant concern associated with conventional puncturing devices is the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries after the puncturing procedure has been completed, as the sharp puncturing tip remains exposed and poses a hazard to both the patient and the medical personnel handling the device. There exists a continuing need for puncturing systems that provide enhanced safety features without compromising the functionality or precision required for successful puncturing procedures.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these safety concerns by providing a puncturing system comprising three primary components arranged in a coaxial, telescoping configuration.

The first component is an **outer tubular body** configured to remain positioned within a body part during the puncturing procedure. This outer tubular body defines a working lumen extending along its length, through which the remaining components of the system are guided. The outer tubular body serves as a stable platform and access conduit, remaining in place within the body part to maintain the established access pathway.

The second component is an **inner tubular body**, which is guided through the working lumen of the outer tubular body. This inner tubular body is configured for independent longitudinal displacement relative to the outer tubular body, meaning it can be advanced or withdrawn along its longitudinal axis without necessarily requiring corresponding movement of the outer tubular body. The inner tubular body itself defines a puncture lumen extending through its length, which serves as a guide channel for the puncturing needle.

The third component is a **puncturing needle**, which is guided through the puncture lumen of the inner tubular body. Like the inner tubular body relative to the outer tubular body, the puncturing needle is capable of independent longitudinal displacement relative to the inner tubular body. This needle includes a sharp puncturing section at its distal end, configured to penetrate tissue and create the necessary access pathway during the puncturing procedure.

## Detailed Operation and Safety Feature

The coordinated, yet independently displaceable, arrangement of these three components enables a critical safety mechanism that distinguishes this invention from conventional puncturing devices.

During the initial phase of the procedure, the puncturing needle is advanced distally beyond the inner tubular body and the outer tubular body to perform the puncturing action, penetrating the target tissue or body part as required by the specific medical procedure. The sharp puncturing section of the needle extends beyond the distal ends of both tubular bodies during this active puncturing phase.

Following successful puncture and completion of the puncturing action, the system enables a safety sequence wherein the inner tubular body is advanced out of the outer tubular body in the distal direction. As the inner tubular body advances relative to the outer tubular body, it moves toward and eventually surrounds the protruding tip of the puncturing needle.

This advancement of the inner tubular body relative to both the outer tubular body and the puncturing needle allows the puncturing needle's tip—including its sharp puncturing section—to be safely accommodated and enclosed within the puncture lumen of the inner tubular body. Because the puncturing needle and inner tubular body are capable of independent longitudinal displacement, this safety-enclosing action can be performed as a deliberate, controlled step following the puncturing procedure, effectively shielding the sharp puncturing section from exposure.

By enclosing the sharp puncturing section within the puncture lumen of the inner tubular body after use, the present invention substantially reduces the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to medical personnel during subsequent handling, disposal, or removal of the puncturing system. The outer tubular body may remain in position within the body part, for example to maintain access for subsequent procedural steps, while the inner tubular body and enclosed needle can be safely managed or removed without exposing the sharp puncturing section.

## Advantages

The puncturing system of the present invention offers several advantages over conventional devices:

1. **Enhanced Safety**: The telescoping arrangement of components allows the sharp puncturing section to be automatically or deliberately shielded after use, minimizing the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries.

2. **Maintained Access**: The outer tubular body can remain within the body part to preserve the established access pathway even after the needle has been safely enclosed, facilitating subsequent procedural steps without requiring re-puncture.

3. **Independent Control**: The independent longitudinal displacement capability of each component provides the operator with precise control over each phase of the procedure, from initial puncture to post-procedure safety enclosure.

4. **Simplified Design**: The coaxial arrangement of tubular bodies provides an elegant, mechanically straightforward solution to the needle-stick safety problem without requiring complex additional mechanisms such as springs, locks, or separate safety sheaths.

5. **Versatility**: This puncturing system may be adapted for use in a variety of medical procedures requiring safe tissue puncture, including but not limited to vascular access, drainage procedures, and biopsy applications.

## Conclusion

The puncturing system described herein represents a significant advancement in the field of medical puncturing devices by providing an integrated, mechanically simple solution for shielding the sharp puncturing section of a needle following use. Through the coordinated, independently displaceable arrangement of an outer tubular body, an inner tubular body, and a puncturing needle, the invention achieves enhanced safety for both patients and medical personnel while maintaining the functional requirements necessary for successful puncturing procedures within a body part.

# The Word "The"

"The" is the most commonly used word in the English language, yet it often goes unnoticed in everyday speech and writing. As the definite article, it plays a crucial grammatical role, distinguishing specific, known entities from general or unspecified ones.

## Grammatical Function

Unlike the indefinite articles "a" and "an," which introduce something new or unspecified, "the" signals that the noun it precedes refers to something particular—something the speaker and listener both understand or have already discussed. For example:

- "I saw a cat" suggests any cat, unspecified.
- "I saw the cat" implies a specific cat, likely known to both parties.

This subtle distinction allows for precise communication, helping listeners and readers track what is being referenced throughout a conversation or text.

## Historical Origins

The word "the" has its roots in Old English, evolving from words like "þe" and "se," which were used as demonstrative pronouns meaning "that" or "this." Over centuries, these forms simplified into the single word we use today, losing much of the inflection that Old English nouns and articles once carried.

## Frequency and Linguistic Importance

Linguists and language analysts consistently rank "the" as the most frequently used word in English texts, appearing far more often than any other word. Its ubiquity makes it a foundational element of English grammar, essential for constructing coherent sentences.

## A Universal Yet Invisible Word

Despite its importance, "the" is rarely the focus of attention. It carries no standalone meaning and cannot exist independently—it must always accompany a noun. Yet without it, English would lose much of its clarity and structure, making communication more ambiguous.

In essence, "the" exemplifies how small, seemingly insignificant words can hold immense power in shaping meaning, providing structure, and enabling precise communication in the English language.

counterfactuals.output:
# TECHNICAL FIELD

The present disclosure relates generally to medical devices used for vascular access, and more particularly to a telescoping catheter assembly incorporating a needle tip safety shielding mechanism configured to automatically enclose a needle tip following insertion into a patient's vasculature, thereby reducing the risk of accidental needlestick injury.

---

## BACKGROUND

Peripheral intravenous ("IV") catheters and similar vascular access devices typically employ an introducer needle disposed within a catheter tube to facilitate percutaneous puncture and subsequent placement of the catheter within a blood vessel. Following successful venipuncture, the introducer needle is withdrawn from the catheter, leaving the catheter in place for fluid administration or blood sampling.

A persistent challenge in the design of such devices is the risk of accidental needlestick injury to clinicians during withdrawal of the needle, which may result in exposure to bloodborne pathogens. Regulatory frameworks, including the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, have driven demand for passive safety mechanisms that do not rely on additional manual actuation steps by the clinician, as such steps are prone to being omitted or improperly performed under clinical time pressure.

Existing safety catheter designs often incorporate needle shields that must be manually activated, or spring-loaded mechanisms that add significant bulk, complexity, and cost to the device. Many such mechanisms are also prone to premature activation, which can compromise the catheter placement procedure, or delayed activation, which fails to adequately protect the clinician. There remains a need for a telescoping catheter assembly that reliably and passively shields the needle tip immediately upon completion of the venipuncture and withdrawal sequence, while maintaining a low-profile, cost-effective, and manufacturable design.

---

## SUMMARY

The present invention provides a telescoping catheter assembly comprising an outer catheter member, an inner needle assembly slidably and telescopically disposed within the outer catheter member, and a safety shielding mechanism configured to automatically translate over and enclose the needle tip upon withdrawal of the needle assembly from the catheter hub, without requiring separate manual actuation by the user.

In one embodiment, the assembly comprises:

- (a) an outer catheter tube having a proximal end, a distal end, and a lumen extending therethrough, the distal end configured for insertion into a blood vessel;
- (b) a catheter hub affixed to the proximal end of the outer catheter tube;
- (c) an introducer needle slidably received within the lumen of the outer catheter tube, the needle having a sharpened distal tip extending beyond the distal end of the catheter tube during an insertion configuration;
- (d) a telescoping shield member disposed coaxially about at least a portion of the needle, the shield member being slidably retained in a retracted position relative to the needle tip during the insertion configuration; and
- (e) a locking mechanism configured to releasably retain the shield member in the retracted position and to automatically permit translation of the shield member to a deployed position, in which the shield member circumferentially encloses the needle tip, in response to relative proximal movement between the needle assembly and the catheter hub exceeding a predetermined threshold displacement.

The telescoping shield member and locking mechanism cooperate to provide a passive, single-use safety feature that activates automatically as a natural consequence of the standard catheter placement workflow—specifically, the withdrawal of the needle from the catheter hub following successful venous cannulation—thereby eliminating reliance on a separate clinician-actuated step.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### General Assembly Configuration

Referring to the assembly in its overall configuration, the telescoping catheter assembly comprises an outer catheter tube (10) having a distal insertion end (12) and a proximal end (14) fixedly engaged with a catheter hub (16). The catheter hub (16) defines a proximal opening (18) sized to slidably receive an inner needle assembly (20).

The inner needle assembly (20) comprises an introducer needle (22) having a sharpened distal tip (24), a needle shaft (26) extending proximally therefrom, and a needle hub (28) affixed to the proximal end of the needle shaft (26). The needle shaft (26) is dimensioned to extend through the lumen of the outer catheter tube (10) such that the sharpened distal tip (24) protrudes distally beyond the distal insertion end (12) of the catheter tube during the insertion configuration, enabling simultaneous venipuncture by the needle and advancement of the catheter tube into the vessel lumen.

### Telescoping Shield Member

Disposed coaxially about the needle shaft (26), intermediate the needle hub (28) and the sharpened distal tip (24), is a telescoping shield member (30). The shield member (30) comprises an elongate tubular body (32) having an inner diameter slightly greater than the outer diameter of the needle shaft (26), permitting axial sliding movement of the shield member (30) relative to the needle shaft (26).

In the insertion configuration, the shield member (30) is retained in a proximal, retracted position by a releasable locking mechanism (34), such that the shield member (30) does not obstruct the sharpened distal tip (24) or interfere with the outer catheter tube (10) during insertion.

The releasable locking mechanism (34) may comprise, in various embodiments:

1. A frictional interference fit between an inner surface of the shield member (30) and a corresponding detent or ridge formed on the needle shaft (26), sized to release upon application of a predetermined proximal withdrawal force;
2. A resilient tab or catch engaging a complementary groove formed in the catheter hub (16), configured to disengage upon relative axial displacement between the needle assembly (20) and the catheter hub (16) exceeding a threshold distance corresponding substantially to the length of the sharpened distal tip (24) plus a safety margin; or
3. A frangible or deformable retention element configured to shear or deform upon application of the withdrawal force typically exerted during clinical removal of the needle assembly from the catheter hub, thereby releasing the shield member for distal translation.

Upon release, a biasing element (36), such as a compression spring or resilient elastomeric sleeve disposed between the needle hub (28) and the proximal end of the shield member (30), urges the shield member (30) distally along the needle shaft (26) until the shield member (30) fully encloses the sharpened distal tip (24).

### Locking Confirmation Feature

In a further embodiment, the shield member (30) includes a distal locking collar (38) configured to engage a complementary retention feature (40) formed at or near the sharpened distal tip (24) upon full distal translation of the shield member. Engagement of the locking collar (38) with the retention feature (40) produces an audible and/or tactile confirmation (e.g., a click) signaling to the clinician that the needle tip (24) has been fully and irreversibly enclosed. The locking collar (38), once engaged, prevents proximal retraction of the shield member (30), thereby providing a permanent, single-use safety enclosure that cannot be inadvertently disengaged to re-expose the needle tip.

### Sequence of Operation

1. **Insertion Configuration:** The clinician grasps the catheter hub (16) and/or needle hub (28) and advances the assembly such that the sharpened distal tip (24), extending beyond the outer catheter tube (10), punctures the skin and vessel wall, permitting advancement of the outer catheter tube (10) into the vessel lumen.

2. **Catheter Placement Confirmation:** Upon observation of a flashback of blood into a flashback chamber in fluid communication with the needle shaft (26), the clinician advances the outer catheter tube (10) further into the vessel while holding the needle assembly (20) stationary, or advances the entire assembly followed by catheter advancement over the needle, according to standard technique.

3. **Needle Withdrawal:** The clinician withdraws the needle assembly (20) proximally relative to the catheter hub (16). This proximal withdrawal motion generates the relative axial displacement necessary to disengage the releasable locking mechanism (34).

4. **Automatic Shield Deployment:** Upon disengagement of the locking mechanism (34), the biasing element (36) drives the shield member (30) distally along the needle shaft (26), enclosing the sharpened distal tip (24) prior to the tip (24) fully exiting the catheter hub (16) and becoming exposed to the environment.

5. **Locking Confirmation:** The distal locking collar (38) engages the retention feature (40), producing a tactile/audible confirmation and permanently securing the shield member (30) in the deployed position over the needle tip (24).

6. **Disposal:** The needle assembly (20), now bearing the deployed and locked shield member (30), is disposed of as a single unit in accordance with standard sharps disposal protocols, with the sharpened distal tip (24) permanently enclosed.

### Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, the telescoping shield member (30) comprises two or more concentrically nested tubular segments configured to sequentially telescope distally relative to one another, thereby providing an extended shielding length sufficient to enclose an elongated needle shaft while maintaining a compact retracted profile during the insertion configuration. This multi-stage telescoping configuration may be particularly advantageous in longer catheter assemblies, such as those used for midline or peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) placement.

In a further alternative embodiment, the biasing element (36) is omitted, and distal translation of the shield member (30) is instead effected manually by the clinician following disengagement of the locking mechanism (34), with the locking mechanism (34) nonetheless configured to prevent proximal re-exposure of the needle tip (24) once the shield member (30) has been advanced to the deployed position, thereby retaining certain passive safety characteristics while reducing device complexity and cost.

In yet another embodiment, the shield member (30) is provided with a visual indicator, such as a color-changing band or window, configured to become visible only when the shield member (30) has reached and locked in the fully deployed position, providing an additional visual confirmation of complete needle tip enclosure independent of tactile or audible feedback.

---

## CLAIMS (Illustrative, Non-Limiting)

**1.** A telescoping catheter assembly comprising:
an outer catheter tube having a proximal end and a distal end and defining a lumen therethrough;
a catheter hub affixed to the proximal end of the outer catheter tube;
a needle assembly slidably disposed within the lumen of the outer catheter tube, the needle assembly comprising a needle shaft having a sharpened distal tip;
a telescoping shield member disposed coaxially about the needle shaft and slidable between a retracted position and a deployed position in which the shield member encloses the sharpened distal tip; and
a releasable locking mechanism configured to retain the shield member in the retracted position during insertion of the needle assembly and to automatically release the shield member for translation to the deployed position in response to proximal withdrawal of the needle assembly relative to the catheter hub.

**2.** The assembly of claim 1, further comprising a biasing element configured to urge the shield member distally toward the deployed position upon release of the locking mechanism.

**3.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the shield member comprises a distal locking collar configured to engage a retention feature disposed proximate the sharpened distal tip upon full distal translation of the shield member, thereby permanently securing the shield member in the deployed position.

**4.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the releasable locking mechanism comprises a frictional interference fit, a resilient catch-and-groove engagement, or a frangible retention element.

**5.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the shield member comprises a plurality of concentrically nested telescoping segments.

**6.** The assembly of claim 3, wherein engagement of the locking collar with the retention feature produces an audible confirmation signal.

**7.** The assembly of claim 1, further comprising a visual indicator configured to become visible upon the shield

# INVENTION SUMMARY

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to medical devices, and more particularly to vascular access devices incorporating nested tubular components configured to shield a needle cannula before, during, and after use, thereby reducing the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to healthcare personnel and patients.

## Background

Vascular access devices, including intravenous (IV) catheters, blood collection needles, and introducer needle assemblies, are widely used in clinical settings for the administration of fluids, medications, and the withdrawal of blood samples. Conventional devices typically expose a sharp needle tip during insertion and, critically, during withdrawal after the procedure is complete. This exposure creates a substantial risk of accidental needle-stick injury, which may result in transmission of bloodborne pathogens such as HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C.

Prior safety devices have attempted to address this problem through various mechanisms, including hinged shields, retractable needles, and sliding sleeves. However, many such solutions suffer from drawbacks including mechanical complexity, unreliable activation, increased device footprint, added manufacturing cost, or failure to provide passive (automatic) needle protection without requiring an additional deliberate action by the user. There remains a need for a vascular access device that provides reliable, passive needle-stick protection while maintaining a low profile and manufacturing simplicity comparable to conventional non-safety devices.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a vascular access device comprising a plurality of nested, telescoping tubular components configured to automatically shield a needle cannula upon withdrawal from a patient's vasculature, without requiring a separate manual activation step by the clinician.

In one embodiment, the device comprises:

1. **An outer tubular member** (or "guard tube") having a proximal end, a distal end, and a lumen extending therethrough, the distal end defining a blunt or rounded tip configured to prevent tissue trauma;

2. **An intermediate tubular member** slidably and coaxially disposed within the lumen of the outer tubular member, the intermediate member being longitudinally translatable between a first, retracted position, in which a distal portion of the intermediate member is housed within the outer tubular member, and a second, extended position, in which the distal portion projects beyond the distal end of the outer tubular member;

3. **A needle cannula** fixedly or slidably disposed within a lumen of the intermediate tubular member, the needle cannula having a sharpened distal tip configured for percutaneous insertion, wherein the sharpened distal tip is exposed beyond the distal end of the intermediate tubular member when the intermediate tubular member is in the extended position, and is fully enclosed within the intermediate and/or outer tubular members when the intermediate tubular member returns to the retracted position;

4. **A biasing element** (e.g., a coil spring, resilient polymer element, or equivalent elastic member) disposed to urge the intermediate tubular member from the extended position toward the retracted position; and

5. **A locking mechanism** configured to releasably retain the intermediate tubular member in the extended position during insertion of the needle cannula into the patient's vasculature, and to release the intermediate tubular member automatically upon withdrawal of the device from the vasculature, such that the biasing element drives the intermediate tubular member — and consequently the needle cannula — into the retracted, shielded position.

In operation, the nested tubular components remain in a locked, extended configuration during needle insertion, permitting normal clinical use of the device. Upon completion of the procedure and withdrawal of the device from the patient, a triggering feature (such as a detent, cam surface, or frictional release element positioned at or near the patient's skin surface) disengages the locking mechanism, permitting the biasing element to translate the intermediate tubular member proximally relative to the outer tubular member. This translation causes the sharpened needle tip to be withdrawn into and shielded by the surrounding tubular members, wherein it is captured and, in certain embodiments, further secured by a secondary locking feature to prevent re-extension.

## Advantages

The nested tubular configuration of the present invention provides several advantages over prior art safety devices, including:

- **Passive protection**: needle shielding occurs automatically upon withdrawal, without requiring a separate manual step by the user, thereby reducing reliance on clinician compliance;
- **Mechanical simplicity**: the telescoping arrangement of concentric tubular members reduces the number of discrete parts relative to hinged or articulated safety shields;
- **Low profile**: the coaxial, nested arrangement maintains a device diameter and length comparable to conventional non-safety vascular access devices;
- **Reliability**: the use of a biasing element and mechanical lock/release mechanism provides consistent, repeatable shielding behavior across manufacturing lots;
- **Compatibility**: the device may be adapted for use with a variety of vascular access procedures, including peripheral IV catheterization, central line introduction, and blood collection.

## Brief Description of Alternative Embodiments

In alternative embodiments, additional nested tubular layers may be incorporated to provide multi-stage shielding (e.g., an inner needle-shielding tube nested within an intermediate catheter-advancement tube, nested within an outer stabilizing sheath). The locking and biasing mechanisms may be implemented using a variety of equivalent structures, including but not limited to: leaf-spring detents, resilient tabs, compressed elastomeric sleeves, magnetic couplings, or shape-memory alloy elements configured to actuate shielding translation upon a change in mechanical load or temperature associated with withdrawal from the patient.

The invention further contemplates visual and/or tactile indicators (e.g., an audible click, color-change window, or palpable detent) configured to confirm to the user that the needle cannula has been fully retracted into the shielded, locked position, providing confirmation that the safety mechanism has properly engaged.

# Patent Abstract

## Title: Safety Puncturing System for Catheter Placement with Sequential Needle Retraction Mechanism

### Abstract

A puncturing system for catheter placement is disclosed, comprising an outer sheath, an inner sheath disposed coaxially within the outer sheath, and a puncturing needle slidably disposed within the inner sheath, wherein the system enables safe retraction of the needle after vascular access is achieved. The outer sheath comprises a catheter tube configured to remain within the vessel during use. The inner sheath is longitudinally movable relative to both the outer sheath and the needle, and includes a needle-guiding lumen. The needle comprises a sharpened distal tip for skin and vessel penetration and a proximal actuation portion connected to a retraction mechanism.

During operation, the needle and inner sheath advance together through the outer sheath to puncture the vessel. Upon confirmation of successful puncture, the inner sheath is held stationary or advanced independently relative to the outer sheath, while the needle is retracted proximally through the inner sheath lumen, such that the sharpened needle tip is withdrawn into and shielded by the inner sheath before the inner sheath itself is retracted from the outer sheath. This sequential, relative motion—wherein the needle retracts first into the inner sheath, and only thereafter does the inner sheath retract relative to the outer sheath—ensures that the exposed sharp tip is never present within the outer sheath or exposed to the operator during withdrawal, thereby preventing needle-stick injury and blood leakage. A locking or interlock mechanism may be provided between the outer sheath, inner sheath, and needle hub to enforce the correct retraction sequence.

---

### Independent Claim 1

A puncturing system for catheter placement, comprising:
an outer sheath having a proximal end, a distal end, and a lumen extending therethrough, the outer sheath configured to be positioned within a body vessel;
an inner sheath disposed within the lumen of the outer sheath and axially movable relative to the outer sheath, the inner sheath having a distal end and defining an inner lumen;
a needle disposed within the inner lumen of the inner sheath and axially movable relative to the inner sheath, the needle having a sharpened distal tip configured to puncture the body vessel;
wherein the needle and the inner sheath are configured to advance distally together relative to the outer sheath to a puncturing position in which the sharpened distal tip extends beyond the distal end of the inner sheath and the distal end of the outer sheath to puncture the body vessel;
and wherein, following puncture, the needle is configured to retract proximally relative to the inner sheath such that the sharpened distal tip is withdrawn to a position proximal of the distal end of the inner sheath, prior to retraction of the inner sheath relative to the outer sheath, thereby shielding the sharpened distal tip within the inner sheath during subsequent withdrawal of the inner sheath from the outer sheath.

### Claim 2 (dependent)
The system of claim 1, further comprising an interlock mechanism configured to prevent proximal retraction of the inner sheath relative to the outer sheath until the needle has been retracted to the position proximal of the distal end of the inner sheath.

### Claim 3 (dependent)
The system of claim 1, wherein the outer sheath comprises a catheter configured to remain indwelling within the body vessel after retraction of the inner sheath and the needle.

### Claim 4 (dependent)
The system of claim 1, further comprising a needle hub coupled to a proximal end of the needle and an actuation member coupled to the needle hub, the actuation member configured to effect proximal retraction of the needle independent of movement of the inner sheath and the outer sheath.

### Claim 5 (dependent)
The system of claim 1, wherein the inner sheath comprises a blood flashback indicator in fluid communication with the inner lumen, the flashback indicator configured to indicate successful puncture of the body vessel.

# CLAIM

**1.** A medical puncturing device configured for partial indwelling within a body, comprising:

a hollow needle assembly having a distal puncturing tip and a proximal end, said needle assembly defining a longitudinal axis and being configured to penetrate tissue to establish vascular or subcutaneous access;

an indwelling catheter member disposed coaxially about at least a portion of said needle assembly, said catheter member configured to remain within the body following withdrawal of said needle assembly therefrom, said catheter member having a distal end positioned proximate the puncturing tip prior to withdrawal and a proximal end coupled to a hub structure;

a protective shielding mechanism operatively associated with said needle assembly, said shielding mechanism comprising:

  (a) a guard element movably disposed relative to said needle assembly between a first position, in which said guard element does not obstruct the puncturing tip, and a second position, in which said guard element substantially encloses said puncturing tip so as to prevent inadvertent contact therewith;

  (b) a biasing element configured to urge said guard element toward said second position; and

  (c) a retention structure configured to maintain said guard element in said first position against the force of said biasing element during insertion of said needle assembly into the body, and to release said guard element automatically upon withdrawal of said needle assembly from said catheter member and the body to a predetermined longitudinal position, thereby permitting said biasing element to translate said guard element into said second position;

wherein said retention structure comprises at least one of a frangible detent, a resilient latch, or a friction-fit interface engaging a housing associated with said hub structure, said retention structure being disengaged solely as a result of relative axial movement between said needle assembly and said housing exceeding a predetermined threshold distance corresponding to substantially complete withdrawal of the puncturing tip from the body; and

wherein said guard element, upon reaching said second position, is further configured to lockingly engage said needle assembly so as to prevent return movement of said guard element from said second position to said first position, thereby permanently covering the puncturing tip after a puncturing procedure has been completed.

**2.** The device of claim 1, wherein said biasing element comprises a compression spring disposed coaxially about said needle assembly between said hub structure and said guard element.

**3.** The device of claim 1, wherein said guard element comprises a tubular sleeve slidably disposed about said needle assembly, said tubular sleeve having a distal opening sized to permit passage of said puncturing tip in said first position and configured to be closed by a resilient flap or septum upon reaching said second position.

**4.** The device of claim 1, further comprising a visual or tactile indicator configured to signal to a user that said guard element has reached said second position and lockingly engaged said needle assembly.

**5.** The device of claim 1, wherein said hub structure further comprises a fluid-tight connector configured for attachment to an external fluid line, said connector remaining in fluid communication with said catheter member after withdrawal of said needle assembly and actuation of said protective shielding mechanism.

**6.** The device of claim 1, wherein said predetermined threshold distance is selected such that said retention structure disengages only after said distal end of said catheter member has been fully seated within the body and said puncturing tip has been withdrawn proximally of said distal end of said catheter member.

**7.** The device of claim 1, wherein said guard element and said retention structure are configured such that disengagement of said retention structure and translation of said guard element into said second position occur automatically, without requiring a separate manual actuation step by a user.
